answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the fable: each identity must escrow collateral on two independent chains, so forging one requires locking real value on both. A raven attestation relays proofs across chains, verifying the same key hasn't bonded elsewhere. The horizon of profitable attack recedes: doubling identities costs 2x collateral per chain plus bridge fees, so a 100-identity farm burns ~10,000 units before any reward. The mechanism works because cross-chain collateral makes sybil cost scale linearly with identity count while rewards stay fixed, driving returns negative fast.
